name: Interpret what a retrieval question needs
summary: An isolated host LLM interprets a question into typed information needs; production retrieval does not call it.

steps.label: Prepare the question and offered meanings
steps.human:
Validate the original question, optional context, known ID candidates, source-scope metadata and a finite catalog for five dimensions. Add only supplied IDs or literal IDs found in the question; an offered ID is a candidate, not a chosen target. Validate again after augmentation and enforce the 50,000-character input bound.

The caller also supplies the actual kernel Scope and caller Actor. source_scope is an echoed metadata claim, not a verified repository revision or permission grant. This experiment grants no repository-read permissions. [Request contract](kernel/contracts/retrieval_needs.py) · [Task builder](integrations/retrieval_needs_llm.py).

All KernelModel objects have defaulted schema_version=1.0. The callable copies original_question to TaskInput.goal. The current TaskInput goal bound is 16,000 characters; this operation retains the stricter 8,000-character retrieval-needs request bound. The archived N03 execution predates that goal-bound increase. Unknown fields are forbidden. source_scope keys in this example are caller data, not mandatory named schema fields.

Input contract: [request JSON Schema](kernel/schemas/leafcutter.retrieval_needs_request.v1.schema.json) and [runtime validators](kernel/contracts/retrieval_needs.py). catalog must contain entity_types, target_ids, required_fields, document_types and relationships; each maps offered labels to meanings. The validators enforce all five keys and grounded targets in addition to JSON Schema.

This is the request member of [saved N03 operational input](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/inputs/N03.input.json). Its literal TQ-500f candidate has already been added. It is not a response or permission grant. The separate Scope and Actor arguments appear in the next step's task example.

steps.label: Start the isolated kernel run
steps.human:
Start KernelService with the experiment-only registry snapshot. Fixed routing selects host.retrieval_needs / interpret_retrieval_needs and the real LangGraph scheduler. Legacy enrichment and entity recognition are explicitly disabled, as are knowledge reads and memory; the limits allow one host operation and zero Jev calls.

This callable exists only when this experimental snapshot is supplied. No default production descriptor or existing retrieval call-site activates it. [Experiment service](integrations/retrieval_needs_llm.py) · [KernelService](kernel/service.py).

This is an internal phase of start_run, not a separate public JSON endpoint. It creates the [work binding and invocation](kernel/contracts/work.py). The public RunEnvelope becomes available after the next step has opened the wait. The experiment snapshot supplies the fixed capability; the caller does not send a capability_id in TaskInput.

The omitted input_payload is the complete request shown in the previous step and is required for this operation. The complete reconstructed TaskInput, including that payload, passes the [TaskInput model](kernel/contracts/task.py). Actual kernel read_roots=[docs] is distinct from the source_scope metadata's longer read_roots list; permissions=[] grants no repository reads. [Controller construction](scripts/evaluate_retrieval_needs_llm.py).

steps.label: Save the request and wait for the host
steps.human:
Compile the typed HostWorkRequest, persist its operational input artifact and packet, then checkpoint waiting_host through LangGraph. RunEnvelope carries run_id; the packet's id is the interaction identity. The packet carries state_revision, output requirements, output JSON Schema and input_artifact_refs. The external host reads the referenced operational input; the kernel does not call a model client.

[RunEnvelope model](kernel/contracts/run.py) · [HostWorkRequest model](kernel/contracts/interaction.py) · [Operational artifact writer](kernel/interaction/packets.py). The operational artifact is a persisted JSON document with a request member, not a second retrieval-needs schema. It records interaction_id, operation, task_template, prompt_fingerprint, request_schema and evidence. The current writer can add a bounded entity_context projection with separate caller_context and registered_capabilities channels, plus clarifications when supplied; policy and receiver budgets can reduce optional context. Disabled recognition still has a disabled checkpoint status. The archived N03 artifact instead has the historical context_enrichment member. Restored historical checkpoints can retain that older channel; this receipt is not a claim that a new run emits the same wrapper. See kernel/entity_projection.py for the current projection boundary.

[Complete saved waiting envelope](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/N03.started.json). The historical temporary artifact path is preserved exactly; [saved N03 operational input](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/inputs/N03.input.json) is the archived readable copy. Selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields are in the linked contract.

steps.label: Interpret all information needs together
steps.human:
Read the packet and referenced input. Interpret selected and uncertain entity types, target IDs, indispensable fields, document types and relationships using only exact offered labels. Also supply detail, completeness, hierarchy and scope-resolution modes, unresolved reasons and a concise rationale. Preserve the original question and source_scope exactly.

Use unresolved reasons for unsupported meanings or unresolved gaps. A discovery need does not itself mean the user must choose a scope. This is one host operation with all dimensions together; the host controls its model and there is no guarantee of one underlying model request. [Host instructions](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py).

Output contract: [output JSON Schema](kernel/schemas/leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1.schema.json) plus [request-bound rules](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py). selections and uncertain each require entity_types, target_ids, required_fields, document_types and relationships, including empty arrays. Values must be exact offered labels; required_fields names indispensable facts, not optional supporting information. Common schema_version defaults to 1.0.

[Complete saved candidate](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/responses/N03.json). The complete typed payload is shown at Return the typed needs. This projection alone is not a valid full output.

steps.label: Submit the interpretation to its wait
steps.human:
Wrap the candidate in an InteractionSubmission for the original run, interaction and expected state revision. Supply actor.kind=host, a valid actor ID, the requested output schema and any actual usage receipt. Send it to KernelService.resume_run. Missing model or token information stays unknown; response.model_id alone is not model provenance.

The [InteractionSubmission model](kernel/contracts/interaction.py) is a transport wrapper around the output. packet.id becomes interaction_id; packet.state_revision becomes expected_state_revision. run_id comes from the envelope. The original request's caller Actor and this responding host Actor have different roles.

The required response field is the complete candidate from the preceding step, unchanged. The actual submission omits usage, so the model defaults it to []; no tokens or model are claimed. [Complete accepted submission](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/N03.submission.json).

steps.label: Check the response before accepting it
steps.human:
Check the current wait, run, revision, host actor and response schema. Validate the payload against the typed schema, then compare it with the actual pending request: question and source_scope must be unchanged; selected and uncertain labels must be offered and must not overlap.

Check that needs_resolution has an explicit reason or a structural gap, and that the combined unresolved reasons will fit the 32-item bound. These deterministic checks establish contract validity, not whether every necessary fact was correctly identified. [Submission checks](kernel/interaction/submissions.py) · [Request-bound checks](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py).

No new wire payload is manufactured here. Successful validation passes the same submission onward; the code's Verdict is an internal Python result, not a JSON field to send. Both [output JSON Schema](kernel/schemas/leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1.schema.json) and the pending request constrain response.

N03 validation projection below shows the actual response facts being checked. Selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields are in the linked contract and complete saved submission.

Changing source_scope.repository would fail request-bound validation even if the JSON Schema still accepts the object. Conversely, [accepted N01](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/N01.result.json) selected test_spec without criteria: its typed response passes these mechanical checks but fails the frozen semantic expectation. Acceptance does not prove the right fields were selected.

steps.label: Record acceptance and resume the run
steps.human:
Persist the accepted submission in the durable interaction ledger before resuming LangGraph. The resumed node validates the same submission again before converting it. Identical accepted replays are idempotent; a conflicting duplicate cannot replace the accepted response. The issued host-operation counter is not evidence of acceptance; the ledger is.

The persisted [SubmissionRecord model](kernel/persistence/base.py) is internal ledger JSON, not a replacement host response. submission stores the complete normalized transport wrapper; the original response body is preserved.

[Complete accepted ledger](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/accepted-ledgers/N03.json). Its required submission member carries the accepted wrapper and response. This record proves acceptance; an issued-operation counter does not.

steps.label: Normalize the interpretation
steps.human:
Recheck the request binding, add structural missing reasons, deduplicate them and derive status: needs_resolution when explicit or structural reasons remain, otherwise decided. Take model_id only from reported host usage; leave it null when unknown. Revalidate the normalized output.

Uncertain alternatives can coexist with decided. discovery_needed does not force needs_resolution; hierarchy_scope=unknown adds a gap only for an exhaustive set or count. These checks normalize a host interpretation; they do not establish semantic correctness. [Normalization](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py).

This phase returns the same [output JSON Schema](kernel/schemas/leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1.schema.json) shape, not a new needs format. Only status, unresolved and model_id are normalized here; the candidate's other fields are retained. The model and request-bound checks are rerun. N03 reported no usage, so no model identity is inferred.

N03's complete candidate and normalized output are equal. Other valid inputs can gain structural unresolved reasons and change status to needs_resolution. A reported model ID that exceeds the output bound can instead cause the existing conversion-failure branch.

steps.label: Return the typed needs
steps.human:
After successful normalization, return the typed payload in a completed CapabilityResult with the interpretation-only limitation. Both decided and needs_resolution are completed interpretation outcomes. Completion does not mean retrieval or an answer finished. A failed normalization terminates through its failure branch instead. [Result conversion](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py).

The internal [CapabilityResult](kernel/contracts/capability.py) uses output_payload. The caller receives a [RunEnvelope](kernel/contracts/run.py), where the same payload is at output.payload and its schema ID is at output.schema_id. Neither wrapper adds a retrieved count. The envelope's completed status is distinct from the payload's decided status.

This is exactly [saved N03 result](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/N03.result.json) at envelope.output.payload. Its top-level fields conform to [output JSON Schema](kernel/schemas/leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1.schema.json). source_scope remains the original metadata claim.

The output examples distinguish the complete typed payload from selected envelope fields; an envelope projection is not a complete response. [Full recorded envelope](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/N03.result.json).

acceptance_scenarios.when: The host controller submits the result
acceptance_scenarios.then: The submission names the original run, interaction, expected revision and output schema with a valid host actor.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An otherwise valid response selects an unoffered ID or changes source_scope
acceptance_scenarios.when: Submission validation checks the actual pending request
acceptance_scenarios.then: The payload is rejected before accepted-ledger persistence; schema validity alone is insufficient for acceptance.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A submission passes schema and request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The durable accepted entry is written before the original LangGraph wait resumes; identical replays do not apply a second interpretation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Accepted output has no structural gaps, no explicit unresolved reasons and no reported host usage
acceptance_scenarios.when: The host operation normalizes the result
acceptance_scenarios.then: The typed output is decided with model_id=null while retaining any uncertain alternatives; this is not a semantic-correctness guarantee.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An offered target ID is neither literal in the question nor supplied in known_ids
acceptance_scenarios.when: The task builder validates the request
acceptance_scenarios.then: The request is refused before host work is opened.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The run is waiting_host and the process restarts
acceptance_scenarios.then: The same persisted wait remains available for its matching response; no new model result is assumed.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A response wrapper carries an invalid actor ID or stale revision
acceptance_scenarios.then: It is refused without accepted-ledger or graph mutation; it is not reported as needs_resolution.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The first pending host payload fails schema or request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The same interaction allows one correction and returns to host interpretation and resubmission without an accepted ledger entry.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An accepted payload retains an unsupported meaning in unresolved
acceptance_scenarios.when: The operation derives its normalized status
acceptance_scenarios.then: The interpretation completes with needs_resolution and its reasons; it neither answers the question nor opens a human wait.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An accepted submission reports a host model ID longer than the output contract allows
acceptance_scenarios.then: It returns a failed capability result without crashing or claiming a completed interpretation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A normalized typed output with decided or needs_resolution
acceptance_scenarios.then: The interpretation completes and returns typed needs with an interpretation-only limitation; no retrieval or final answer is produced.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The first invalid payload was rejected and the one allowed correction was requested
acceptance_scenarios.when: A second payload fails schema or request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The work item fails and the wait is removed without an accepted submission or completed interpretation result.

provenance.note:
Search and scope
Searched artifacts[], by_component and by_flow: the existing retrieval journey and its query, search, traversal, build and baseline artifacts do not describe this callable interpreter. Extend [the existing draft](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#interpret-needs) with an explicitly proposed/unwired call-site; keep implementation detail in this bounded child. The current baseline only links it as separate experiment evidence. No new screens, entities, AC links or approvals are invented. Built means the isolated experiment exists in this worktree; readiness remains draft. The displayed normalize/return phases describe existing conversion code, not new runtime steps. The Atlas schema records branch origins only; return routes are explicit in branch text and links.

Input contract
leafcutter.retrieval_needs_request.v1: original_question; optional context, known_ids and source_scope; catalog with exactly entity_types, target_ids, required_fields, document_types and relationships. Each dimension maps offered labels to meanings, at most 64 labels. Scope and caller Actor are separate TaskInput parameters; permissions are empty. Catalog meanings describe possible information needs, not evidence that a backend can retrieve them.

The builder preserves literal/supplied target candidates. Context and known IDs are unverified hints. Echoing source_scope does not verify its repository, paths or revision. [Typed contracts](kernel/contracts/retrieval_needs.py) · [Frozen example input](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/inputs/N03.input.json).

Output contract and example
leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1 returns the unchanged question/scope, selections and uncertain arrays for all five dimensions, detail_mode, completeness, hierarchy_scope, scope_resolution, unresolved, rationale, engine=host_llm, normalized status and model_id.

Saved N03 input: Count all L2 and L3 descendants of TQ-500f, excluding only TQ-500f, grouped by work_status.
Saved output: entity_types=[ac]; target_ids=[TQ-500f]; required_fields=[level, work_status]; document_types=[ac_yaml]; relationships=[all_descendants]. detail_mode=fields; completeness=exhaustive_count; hierarchy_scope=exclude_root; scope_resolution=sufficient. All uncertain arrays and unresolved are empty; status=decided; model_id=null. This identifies what a later retrieval would need; it returns no count. [Original response](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/responses/N03.json).

Mode meanings
Detail: fields = requested facts; full_document = the whole selected item; bounded_context = the selected item plus requested surroundings; unknown retains a gap. Completeness: single_entity, selected_entities, exhaustive_set, exhaustive_count, examples or unknown. Hierarchy: not_applicable, exclude_root, exclude_parents, include_root or unknown. Scope resolution: sufficient, discovery_needed, user_choice_missing or unknown.

Normalization adds missing entity/document types, unknown detail/completeness, missing fields for fields mode, missing target IDs for identified targets, unresolved user choice/unknown scope, unknown hierarchy for exhaustive sets/counts, and selected_entities with only one target and no relationship. Nonempty uncertain arrays alone do not force needs_resolution. These are structural rules, not an oracle for semantic correctness.

Frozen evidence, not a runtime grading step
The [accepted trial](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/README.md) and [per-case results](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/results.md) record 12 durable accepted submissions and 12 completed interpretations, but only 8/12 frozen semantic passes. N01, N09 and N11 selected test_spec without required criteria for exact-AC obligations. N10 honestly retained unsupported payroll needs but used a prefixed explanation instead of the frozen exact needs_outside_catalog marker. It passed kernel acceptance and failed that semantic encoding check.

The separate prospective overlay passed 7/7 applicable host cases; it does not repair the four shared failures. Original Jev score remains 7/12. Reported deterministic coverage is 76 tests plus 82 subtests, including 18 new controlled cases. No tests or model trial are rerun by this flow; these are dated annotations. [Independent review](docs/analysis/retrieval-needs-llm-probe-2026-10-03/independent-review.md).

Boundaries and provenance
The external host chooses/configures its model; no Haiku or provider client is hardcoded here. The blind trial used a Codex host agent. Its exact model, underlying request count and tokens were unknown. One issued host operation is not one model HTTP call or an accepted response; ledger evidence establishes acceptance.

This flow does not select or run search methods, construct query arguments, retrieve source data, answer the question, call Jev, approve or train classifiers, self-learn, or activate fallback policy. Acceptance and decided are not guarantees of semantic correctness. [Architecture contract](docs/analysis/retrieval-needs-llm-probe-2026-10-03/contract-and-architecture.md).
